html:
Mauri was the Latin name for the Berber people of Mauretania, in what is now northern Morocco and western Algeria. It is the origin of the English word "Moors". On this map they are shown in 700, the moment of the Arab conquest.

After Roman rule faded, the Mauri lived in Berber kingdoms and tribal confederations, some of them Christian, such as the Kingdom of Altava. Around 700 the armies of the Umayyad Caliphate, under Musa ibn Nusayr, reached the Atlantic and brought them under Muslim rule. Many Berbers converted and joined the armies.

In 711 a Berber commander, Tariq ibn Ziyad, led a largely Berber force across the strait into Spain and began the conquest that created al-Andalus. From then on Europeans called the Muslims of Spain and North Africa "Moors".
